speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the public feedback so far since the implementation of a ban on PMD use at void decks and common corridors at 15 towns on 1 September 2019; (b) whether the number of reported incidents has dropped since the implementation; and (c) whether the ban has had any impact on food and goods delivery during the last one month.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On 21 September, a young e-scooter rider collided with an elderly cyclist, Mdm Ong Bee Eng, at Bedok North Street 3.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are deeply saddened by the incident and would like to offer our deepest condolences to Mdm Ong’s family.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This particular accident happened not on a pedestrian footpath, but on a dedicated cycling path where the speed limit is 25 kilometres per hour (km/h).

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Furthermore, the e-scooter was an unregistered and non-compliant device.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It was bought online and that particular device model can go up to 80 km/h.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This accident has caused public alarm over the dangers that personal mobility devices (PMDs) pose to others and has heightened fears for the safety of pedestrians using footpaths, particularly the old and the young.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: With PMD use increasing, the number of accidents involving PMDs has gone up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need footpaths to be safe for pedestrians again.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are determined to improve footpath safety back to the levels we had before PMDs were allowed onto footpaths.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On 5 August 2019, Senior Minister of State for Transport Dr Lam Pin Min explained in this House our plans to strengthen public path safety and reduce PMD-related fire risks.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Given the recent developments, we will revisit these plans to see where we need to rethink our approach and to introduce additional measures.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Please give us a month or two to do this thorough review.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: PMDs are useful devices for first-and-last mile connectivity, if they are used responsibly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But their usage must not endanger device users and pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Ideally, there should be a clear separation of traffic – pedestrians on footpaths, active mobility devices on dedicated paths for PMDs and bicycles, and motor vehicles on roads.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Because of infrastructure constraints, we allow pedestrians and bicycles to use footpaths as a second best practical solution.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: New towns will allow such separation, but existing towns currently do not have many dedicated paths for PMDs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This poses an immediate challenge for PMD users.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is working with Members of Parliament to identify hotspots where we can do something quickly to improve safety, for example, by widening footpaths and installing speed-regulating strips.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will also speed up development of dedicated paths for PMDs and bicycles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Full implementation of such infrastructure enhancements will take time, years.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Meanwhile, we have to make a decision on where to allow PMDs to be used, other than on dedicated paths for PMDs and bicycles – on footpaths, or on roads, or not at all until the town is ready?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will re-examine them and rediscuss with the stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In the meantime, we strongly urge PMD users to be extra responsible and mindful of others.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If their behaviour does not improve, we may have no choice but to ban their usage completely from Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Meanwhile, LTA is working with the Town Councils to implement Pedestrian Only Zones (POZs) at all town centres.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As there are implementation details to iron out, we will create POZs in stages.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will do so as soon as the Town Councils are ready.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about public feedback on the 15 Town Councils’ ban of bicycles, power-assisted bicycles and PMDs in void decks and common property areas.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There have been mixed reactions, with some welcoming the move to enhance safety and others expressing concerns about reduced connectivity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There has not been a noticeable drop in reported incidents yet, as we are still in a two-month advisory period until 31 October 2019.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We expect the full impact to be clearer after the Town Councils begin enforcement action.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: With regard to Mr Yam's question about the impact on food and goods delivery, LTA does not have such statistics.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we have not received adverse feedback from delivery companies, as deliveries are largely done via motorcycles and delivery vehicles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Beyond mandatory inspections at the point of registration, e-scooters will be called up for inspections every two years.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA is studying upstream measures, including import controls, to tackle the problem of non-compliant PMDs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: LTA is also reviewing the penalties for illegal modification of PMDs and other offences.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about the costs of LTA's early disposal incentive for non-UL2272 devices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We strongly urge owners of non-UL2272 devices to come forward early with their devices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Every non-UL2272 device safely disposed of is one less potential fire risk.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I understand that some depend on PMDs for their livelihoods, but this cannot be at the expense of the safety of millions of pedestrians using the footpaths.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The second question is, can LTA get PMD owners to display their registration numbers clearly, big-big, in front and at the back of their PMDs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Recently, I was trying to look for the number, but I could not find it!

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The third question is, will the Ministry take action against shops or individuals who help to do the modifications?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The fourth question is, will the Ministry consider making speed limiter installation compulsory so that it will cut off when the PMDs exceed allowable speeds?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Lastly, what is the recourse for victims of hit-and-run accidents caused by PMDs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I have just received feedback from my resident – his grandparents were hit by PMD riders at night and the youngsters did not stop to help the poor grandparents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Indeed, with respect to the Member's first question, there are opportunities for livelihood and jobs created through the use of PMDs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We want to get the right balance between responsible behaviour and making sure that our public spaces are safe for everybody.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: She mentioned mandatory licensing, a test involving the equivalent of a highway code as well as third-party insurance.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, as we undertake a thorough review of our process, we will be including many of these ideas in that process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For the display of the registration number, indeed, the registration number is supposed to be very prominently displayed.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The reality is that there are many unlicensed PMDs that are still on our paths, on our roads, on our Park Connectors, and which is why, perhaps, the Member was unable to detect the registration number easily.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The registration numbers of properly registered devices are to be properly displayed so that action can be taken against errant riders if necessary.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, then, we will also work to find and take action against those businesses that do this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Compulsory speed limit would potentially be possible if we had access to every device, and again, it is something that we will study comprehensively.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The Member asked about the recourse as the fifth question, having had the experience of a hit-and-run.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, the Police and LTA – depending on the exact location and the exact circumstances – will try to put together information from whatever sources we have to catch the perpetrators.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But ultimately, the key message is that in all of these issues, what we are dealing with is a small number of very irresponsible and dangerous individuals.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We need to find a way to educate them, to enforce against them when they act in this way and try to find ways to develop a new safety culture in our public spaces so that people can have the assurance of a safe experience on the footpaths.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, going forward, any new device would need to be compliant and registered with our current framework.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the likelihood is that what we are dealing with is the errant behaviour by people who have previously brought in very large devices, very fast devices or have illegally modified the devices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But given the number of these devices that are already here in Singapore, on our footpaths and on our roads, there are other steps that we need to consider for early intervention in the first place.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
